To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of pipelined applications running on a time-shared cluster can be improved significantly by using a simple, yet effective technique called application-specific scheduling.

the scheduling of best-effort and hard real-time applications can be done efficiently and effectively by using a combination of static and dynamic scheduling techniques, and that the performance of a system that runs such applications is significantly better than a system that runs either best-effort or hard real-time applications alone.

(1) the scheduling algorithms that are currently used for real-time systems do not scale well for large clusters; (2) the best-effort and soft-real-time systems that are currently used in clusters are not suitable for time-shared clusters; and (3) a combination of scheduling and resource management techniques is required for time-shared clusters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of cluster architectures that are capable of meeting the diverse QoS requirements of applications running in time-shared environments.
the design of cluster architectures that can support diverse applications with different QoS requirements, while ensuring that the applications do not interfere with the other applications.
the design and implementation of a system that supports the execution of a variety of real-time and best-effort applications on time-shared high-performance clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the performance of a parallel application is a function of the underlying hardware architecture (number of nodes, interconnection network etc.), the application characteristics (number of processors needed, data distribution, communication pattern etc.) and the operating system (scheduling, memory management etc.).
clusters are being deployed for a wide variety of applications, and the applications have diverse requirements, which need to be satisfied by the underlying systems.
a cluster needs to support a wide range of applications, with varying characteristics and QoS requirements, in a time-shared fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to schedule best-effort and hard-real time tasks in a time-shared cluster, while guaranteeing the QoS requirements of the tasks.
we are developing a framework for scheduling best-effort and soft real-time applications on time-shared cluster systems.
we have developed a framework for designing and implementing a cluster-based parallel system that can support multiple applications with diverse characteristics in a time-shared fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a pipelined application on a cluster is determined by the performance of the pipeline stages and the communication between them.
a single system architecture cannot cater to all applications.
the design and implementation of high performance parallel applications on clusters needs to be done in a way that is cognizant of the underlying system architecture.
